motion.purpose: A step that settles exponentially, with no overshoot.

narrative.overview:
The engine's own data book, printed on flat paper, with one amber mark. The site draws the engine as its engineers already draw it: timing diagrams, page maps, distribution bars and latency plots, on paper over a flat ground. The look names nothing on screen: every object carries the engine's own name, and the picture is the engine's own diagram.

The system is a bright one. It ships a single light scheme, paper under daylight, plus a more-contrast variant and a forced-colours mapping; there is no dark scheme. Density is a reference book's: a calm reading column on one sheet, diagrams on a faint graticule, tables and readouts in tabular figures, a run-in head beside its first paragraph. Colour is spent as meaning only: amber for now, the second ink for what must not be missed, and six fills, each with its glyph or hatch, as the one colour code.

Motion keeps to the action. Things move when the learner acts and are still between actions, and every duration is 0 under reduced motion, with the state drawn at its end. Data Book replaced The Pass, the kitchen world the course was first drawn in, on 2026-11-16 (D-062); nothing of that world is drawn any more.
keyCharacteristics: A flat ground with no texture, and paper cut square with one soft sheet shadow.
Amber means now: it has three carriers, always with its dark edge, a shape and a word.
Focus is ink: 3 px of text-1 at a 2 px offset, with a paper halo.
Three faces: Big Shoulders Display for titles, Atkinson Hyperlegible for reading and labels, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for code and every number.
Sentence case everywhere: nothing is transformed to upper case, so vLLM, SGLang and v0.33.0 keep their casing.
Six fills with their glyphs are the one colour code, and appear only where the model's state is drawn.
One instrument frame for every game and one template for every lesson, so the way on is always in the same place.
3D is a model of the same diagram: matte solids on a pale base, with every word and number in DOM over it.

rules.name: The One Marker Rule
rules.body: Amber means now. It has three carriers and no others: the control to act on now, the "now" cursor on a diagram, and the current-position mark in the rail and on the course track. The header's Continue is an outline wherever the page has a move in hand, and an intro's callouts are ink discs.

rules.name: The Ink Focus Rule
rules.body: The focus ring is 3 px of text-1 at a 2 px offset, with a paper halo. It is never amber, so focus is not mistaken for now, and it reads against the amber button's own edge. Where focus is sent so that reading starts there, not to a control: a verdict or a result takes the ring at a 6 px offset, clear of its words, and a page or a game's whole section takes none.

rules.name: The Colour Is State Rule
rules.body: A code colour appears only where the model's state is drawn, and always with its glyph or hatch.

rules.name: The Declared Pair Rule
rules.body: A foreground goes on a background only through a pair tokens.ts declares and verify-tokens checks: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for marks and edges, in both shipped schemes.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No text is transformed to upper case, anywhere. Engine names keep their own casing.

rules.name: The Ramp Rule
rules.body: A size is a step of the ramp: `font-size` takes a `--es-size-*` token or a type role's own size, and a size outside the ramp is a one-off that keeps a one-line comment saying why.

rules.name: The Short Viewport Rule
rules.body: Under 600 px of viewport height nothing is sticky or pinned. An instrument's dock on a narrow screen is pinned only from 700 px.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: No texture anywhere. One shadow for a sheet and one for a popover. Paper is cut square.

rules.name: The Moves On Step Rule
rules.body: Things move on an action and are still between actions: 120 ms for the hand, 240 ms for a step, 640 ms for the one authored moment of an instrument. A readout changes at once and shows its delta for one second. Every duration is 0 under reduced motion, and the state is drawn at its end.

rules.name: The Words Are DOM Rule
rules.body: Every word or number a learner reads in a 3D scene is DOM over the canvas; a texture carries only marks nobody needs to read.

rules.name: The Quiet Provenance Rule
rules.body: One stamp per instrument, table or figure. A tag inside prose is a dotted underline.

dos: **Do** take every colour, face, shadow, radius and duration from a token role in src/design/tokens.ts; tokens.css is generated from it and verify-tokens fails when they disagree.
**Do** keep amber for now alone, on its three carriers, always with its dark edge, a shape and a word.
**Do** draw focus as 3 px of text-1 at a 2 px offset, with a paper halo.
**Do** set every number the learner compares in the mono face with tabular figures, with its tag.
**Do** give every category its fill and its glyph, and carry yellow and white marks on their edge colour.
**Do** give every `font-size` a step of the size ramp and every radius a step of the rounded scale; a deliberate one-off keeps a one-line comment saying why.
**Do** put a game in the instrument frame and a lesson in the lesson template, with the diagram, the current control and the readout on one screen.
**Do** give every target 44 px on its short side, and draw a small mark small inside it.
donts: **Don't** add a dark scheme; the system ships light and more-contrast only.
**Don't** lay a texture, a highlight or a gradient sheen on any surface; a gradient draws a graticule or a hatch and nothing else.
**Don't** colour anything for decoration, or make a selected, current or focused thing amber.
**Don't** fade text with opacity to show a state; use the quiet text role, which keeps 4.5:1.
**Don't** use Unicode characters or an icon font as icons; draw them on the 24-unit grid.
**Don't** put a word or a number a learner reads into a 3D texture, or light a scene with anything but its one key and its hemisphere.
**Don't** pin or stick anything under 600 px of viewport height.
